text:
morgan: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change we see a new tail on token latency for a subset of routes. Token-level waterfall shows frequent kernel handoffs around token 12-18 and a spike in KV cache misses. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/7G1/runtime-token-breakdown?panel=13

sanjay: saw that too. SM occupancy drops right after the handoff, VRAM stays steady but power & thermal briefly spike on a single MIG slice. probably kernel hotpath thrash.

elaine: can you paste the perf trace? small snippet is fine. also which routes hit it — internal/large-context or public-chat?

morgan: paste below (trimmed):
```
# perf trace snippet (runtime-profiler)
route: /chat/long-context
seq_len: median 320
tokens: 0..40
events:
  - kernel_select: kernel_v2_fast
  - kv_prefetch: miss (backend cold)
  - kernel_select: kernel_v1_fallback
  - kv_load: delayed 4ms
  - emit_token: +12ms
```

nanya: interesting that kv_prefetch shows miss then delayed load. if prefetch policy batches by request arrival it can race with kernel switch and K/V cache warming.

kevin: can we correlate with batcher logs? maybe the batching heuristic moved a request to a different slice to reduce latency but forced a kernel incompatible with current KV layout.

perf-bot: auto-alert: token_tail_95 increased 2.3x on route /chat/long-context between 1972460000 and 1972467000. attached: perf-correlation table.

morgan: I looked at per-route KPIs: error rates unaffected, but per-token cost up ~8% for that route. The fallback kernel increases compute on SMs while prefetch stalls, so occupancy dives (cuda_sm_occupancy drops from 72% -> 28%) and thermal telemetry shows a short 6°C rise localized to MIG slice 2.

elaine: that's consistent with kernel having a different register pressure and triggering more frequent evictions — VRAM fragmentation could be a factor. Any eviction logs?

morgan: eviction logs show small KV chunk evictions at the same time: "evict shard=3 size=128KB reason=fragmentation". kvcache hit ratio dips 14%.

anya: proposal: add a dashboard panel that stitches token waterfall + batcher decision + kernel selection timeline. Right now panels are separate and aligning them manually is slow.

kevin: +1. also add a per-MIG-slice thermal/SM occupancy heatmap for the slice that served the request. that'd help spot slice-localized regressions.

elaine: short-term mitigation: tune batcher to prefer same-kernel grouping when possible (prefer kernel affinity) and delay prefetch by 2ms when we detect a kernel selection change in-flight, to avoid prefetch losing locality. Might cost micro-latency for cold requests but reduce tail.

morgan: agree. I'll open a small canary that flips kernel-affinity=on for the impacted route only. If we see token_tail_95 drop within 30m we can roll to prod.

perf-bot: action_created: perf/1972467890 - canary: kernel-affinity for /chat/long-context. owner: morgan.

infra-bot: FYI we have quota on how many canaries can run per region; this one is scheduled on west1 only.

kevin: telemetry tasks: 1) add combined waterfall+batches+kernels panel (grafana), 2) per-MIG-slice occupancy/thermal heatmap, 3) KV eviction scatter by time. I'll pick up (1).

anya: I'll prototype the delayed-prefetch toggle and a test harness to simulate kernel handoffs with synthetic traces.

elaine: pairing note: if the kernel switch is necessary due to sequence-length branching, we should also consider a cheap kernel compatibility layer that accepts prefetch pointers across kernels (avoid stale invalidation). Longer term but could be valuable.

morgan: current plan and checks: - deploy kernel-affinity canary to west1 (morgan) - monitor token_tail_95, kv_hit_ratio, per-MIG thermal for 60m - if token_tail_95 falls >=30% revert automatically or roll forward on success.

kevin: tagging dashboard owners: @elaine for occupancy panels, @anya for KV panels, @morgan for route-level KPIs.

morgan: thanks — will post updates. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: reminder in 30m: check perf/1972467890 canary metrics.
